behaviour.summary: The read surface refuses an unauthenticated request with 403 and an empty body. The credential is a per-site header token issued by the cinema in its own back office; there is no anonymous read tier, no scope negotiation and no discovery of what the token would have permitted.
behaviour.testable_as: GET https://api.us.veezi.com/v1/session with no VeeziAccessToken header returns 403 and a zero-length body.
behaviour.consequence_for_agents: The boundary is authorised per site, so an agent acting across an estate holds N credentials obtained through N conversations, and a refusal carries no machine-readable reason distinguishing absent credential from revoked one. CHANGEOVER's answer is a typed refusal with a remediation, not a bare status.

half_life_basis: A live deployment's authentication behaviour can change on any release, and nothing announces it. Ninety days is roughly one vendor release cadence; past that the observation is history, not evidence.

citation.quote: To make a call to any of the Veezi API methods you must add the access token to a custom HTTP header VeeziAccessToken. If this is not provided or if the access token is not valid you will receive a 403 Forbidden HTTP reposonse.

evidence.assertion: The documented refusal is the observed refusal: 403, empty body, no WWW-Authenticate challenge and no problem document.

notes: Probed without credentials against a surface the vendor's own help pages publish as the public entry point. No token was held, sought or used.
